qualitative.filing_summary_10k: For fiscal 2025, Chipotle reported total revenue of $11.9 billion, up 5.4% year-over-year, while comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7% due to a 2.9% decline in transactions partly offset by higher average check. The company opened 334 new company-owned restaurants (ending the year with 4,042) and 11 partner-operated restaurants, with digital sales at 36.7% of food and beverage revenue. Diluted EPS was $1.14, up 2.7% from 2024, and management expects roughly flat comparable sales in 2026 with 350-370 planned restaurant openings.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: For the quarter and six months ended June 30, 2026, Chipotle reported total revenue of $3.35 billion and $6.44 billion, respectively, both up from the prior-year periods, but net income declined to $403.5 million (Q2) and $706.4 million (six months) from $436.1 million and $822.7 million a year earlier. Diluted EPS was $0.32 for the quarter and $0.55 for the six months, versus $0.32 and $0.61 in the comparable 2025 periods. The balance sheet shows retained earnings turned to an accumulated deficit of $67.2 million as of June 30, 2026, down from $619.9 million retained earnings at year-end 2025, alongside continued common stock repurchases.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated September 14, 2026, discloses that Chipotle's Board of Directors increased its size to 11 directors and elected Sabir Sami, a former Yum! Brands executive (including CEO of the KFC Division), as an independent director effective immediately; he was not appointed to any board committees. The filing includes a press release announcing the election as an exhibit.
qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K emphasizes a differentiated brand built on 'Food with Integrity,' registered trademarks ('Chipotle,' 'Responsibly Raised,' etc.), protected trade dress, and food-safety leadership that the company says resonates with guests and supports competitive advantage. However, the Risk Factors section itself notes that many competitors now make similar quality/no-preservative claims, which 'may lessen our differentiation,' indicating the brand-based moat is real but not unassailable.
red_flags: Comparable restaurant sales declined 1.7% in 2025, driven by a 2.9% drop in transactions
Company states it 'may have higher risk for food safety incidents than some of our competitors' due to fresh, unprocessed produce and raw chicken handling
Risk factors acknowledge competitors' similar 'quality ingredient' claims could lessen Chipotle's brand differentiation
Ongoing wage-and-hour litigation and a second NYC audit of Fair Workweek/Earned Safe and Sick Time Act compliance that could result in additional liabilities
Reliance on third-party delivery (over 16% of 2025 food and beverage revenue) carries profitability and reputational risk outside the company's control
2025 tariffs added an estimated ~15 basis points to food, beverage and packaging costs on an ongoing basis
